title: Together
tagline: A social events app for Jönköping University students — post what you are doing, see who is up for it.

hero.alt: The Together events feed on a phone, showing a highlighted event with attendee avatars above a grid of smaller events open at the university
hero.caption: The demo mode, seeded with sample events so the link works without signing up.

problem: Someone is doing something tonight — a pre-game, a gym session, a study circle — and wants other students to come. Group chats bury it under everything else, and event platforms are far too heavy for a Tuesday evening at university.
Together is the narrow version of that: post what you are doing, see who is up for it.
data: Student accounts, events with a time and a place, and who has said they are going. Nothing is scraped and nothing comes from the university — the content is whatever students post.
The public link runs in a demo mode seeded with sample events, so anyone can open it and look around without creating an account.
built: A Next.js front end against a FastAPI backend on MySQL. Students register, post an event with a time and a location, and browse what is open — a feed that separates what is happening soon from everything else, a map view built on Leaflet, and a notification when someone asks to join something you are hosting.
Authentication is JWT with seven-day tokens and bcrypt-hashed passwords; client state is kept in Zustand and persisted to local storage so a refresh does not log you out or lose your place.
result: The app is deployed and open: the link above runs a demo mode seeded with sample events, so anyone can look around the feed, the map and an event page without creating an account.
technical: Next.js 14 with the App Router and Tailwind on the front, FastAPI with SQLAlchemy 2.0 on Python 3.11 behind it, MySQL 8 underneath. The map uses Leaflet with CARTO dark tiles to match the interface rather than fighting it.
The repository is private, so there is no code link on this page — the live demo is the whole of what is public.
